source: no published source; read from the installed 2.1.4 plugin.dylib, which carries full local symbols

lines: Two low-frequency oscillators, each giving the same wave on four outputs spaced apart in phase, with the second running at a fixed ratio of the first
Note — Each of the eight outputs has a lamp beside it which shows green while that output is above 0V and red while it is below.
Sets the rate of the master oscillator, on a scale of 0 to 10
Sets the rate of the second oscillator against the first, in seven steps running from an eighth of it up to eight times it
Restarts both oscillators from the beginning of their cycles each time it is pressed
Switches all eight outputs between swinging either side of 0V and running upwards from 0V; the maker's tooltip for it reads RESET, which is the name of the button above
Chooses which of the four shapes drawn around the knob the master oscillator's four outputs carry
Chooses which of the four shapes drawn around the knob the second oscillator's four outputs carry
Sets the phase spacing of the master oscillator's four outputs, from 0 to 90 degrees; they come out at zero, one, two and three times this
Sets the phase spacing of the second oscillator's four outputs, from 0 to 90 degrees; they come out at zero, one, two and three times this
Adds to the master rate knob, with the total held between 0 and 10
Adds whole steps to the ratio between the two oscillators, one step per volt, counting only voltages above 0V and stopping at eight times the master rate
Adds to the phase spacing of the master oscillator, 9 degrees per volt
Adds to the phase spacing of the second oscillator, 9 degrees per volt
Restarts both oscillators from the beginning of their cycles when it rises past 5V
The master oscillator's wave with no phase offset
The master oscillator's wave shifted by one phase spacing
The master oscillator's wave shifted by two phase spacings
The master oscillator's wave shifted by three phase spacings
The second oscillator's wave with no phase offset
The second oscillator's wave shifted by one phase spacing
The second oscillator's wave shifted by two phase spacings
The second oscillator's wave shifted by three phase spacings
Menu — High Quality (use more CPU) : true, false — works both oscillators out on every sample; with it off they are worked out once every sixteen samples and the gaps interpolated

TwinQuartet-LFO.notes: HORA PUBLISH NO SOURCE, BUT THIS BINARY IS NOT UNREADABLE. nm on the installed 2.1.4 plugin.dylib returns 491 symbols, 116 of them exported, including quadraLFO::process, quadraLFO::quadraLFO, quadraLFOWidget::appendContextMenu and the whole Vult-generated DSP layer (VultEngine_quadraTLFO, QuadraTLFO_DualQuadraLFO, Util_cvToRate and the rest). Everything in this entry was read from that code; nothing was taken from the maker's manual page. PARAMETER 1 IS NOT A RESET. Its configParam name is the string RESET, the same name given to parameter 7, but process reads it at +0x440c and uses it only to choose between two output scalings: at zero the eight outputs are the raw value times 5, so plus and minus 5V, and at one they are the value times 5 plus 5, so 0V to 10V. Its widget sits at census position 116.9,170.4, between the two waveform knobs, where the panel art draws a sine resting on a line and a sine crossing a line. It comes up at zero, the bipolar setting. The actual reset is parameter 7, a momentary button configured 0 to 10 and tested against 5 at +0x44b8, in parallel with the reset input. INDEX ORDER IS NOT PANEL ORDER FOR THE OUTPUTS. Each quad of jacks is laid out as a square and numbered clockwise: index 0 top left, 1 top right, 2 bottom right, 3 bottom left, and the same for 4 to 7. The panel prints 0 degrees, 1X, 2X and 3X beside them, which is the phase multiple each carries, and the tags follow the positions rather than the numbering. Parameter ranges from the constructor: FREQ 0.0001 to 10 with a default of 5; FREQ DIVIDER 0 to 6 with a default of 0, offset by -3 in process to give -3 to +3; WAVEFORM 1 and 2 each 1 to 4 with a default of 1; PHASE 1 and 2 each 0 to 90 degrees with a default of 90, so a new module is already in quadrature. Sixteen lights are configured, two per output, driven as a red and green pair from the sign of that output. The menu carries one item, High Quality, saved in the patch under the key HQ; with it off the DSP runs once every sixteen samples and process interpolates between the last two results at +0x4634.
